claims.statement: apps/server has a single test entrypoint, `pnpm --filter server test` (a bare `vitest run`), governed by one config that includes `tests/**/*.test.ts` in the node environment with 30 s test and hook timeouts, `fileParallelism: false`, and `globalSetup: ["./tests/integration/global-setup.ts"]`; the tree splits into a database-free unit half (8 files / 75 cases) and a database-backed integration half (7 files / 63 cases).

File-level parallelism is disabled because the integration files share one real Postgres database; the config comment states that concurrent files would corrupt each other's counts and assertions, so files run strictly one at a time.

Global setup sequences three operations before any test file runs — recreateTestDatabase(), sweepMainDatabaseStrays(), captureBaselineState() — and returns Vitest's teardown function, which restores the captured baseline and then destroys the test database.

recreateTestDatabase() issues `drop database if exists komyuter_test with (force)` and `create database komyuter_test` over the dev connection (a maintenance connection, because DROP DATABASE can neither run inside a transaction nor target the connection's own database), then on the fresh test database creates the `auth` schema and a stub `auth.users (id uuid primary key, email text)` table before replaying migrations — required because Supabase Auth owns the real `auth.users` in the main database while migration 0002 adds the `admin_users.user_id → auth.users(id) on delete cascade` foreign key.

The test database's schema is exactly the migration history: `supabase/migrations` is read, `*.sql` files are kept and sorted by filename, and each file's text is executed in order on the clean database (starting with the PostGIS extension migration). `drizzle.config.ts` generates migrations into that same directory, so drift between `src/db/schema.ts` and the migrations surfaces as an integration failure; `supabase/seed.sql`, which is a `supabase db reset` concern, is not applied, so the test database has no seeded default fare configuration.

After replaying migrations the test database is seeded with an admin reference: the id of the main database's `auth.users` row matching `ADMIN_EMAIL` is inserted into the test database as a stub auth user plus an `admin_users` row, so the `/api/admin` guard resolves as in dev. If no main-database user matches `ADMIN_EMAIL` the whole insert block is skipped silently, and admin-gated cases then fail with the guard's 401/403 responses instead of a setup error.

sweepMainDatabaseStrays() deletes main-database auth users whose email matches `%@komyuter.test` before the baseline is captured, as the remedy for users left behind by previously interrupted runs; the same `@komyuter.test` suffix is the creation convention for every identity the suite makes (createTestAdmin's `admin-<uuid>@komyuter.test`, createNonAdminToken's `nonadmin-<uuid>@komyuter.test`), it leaves the `@komyuter.ph` seeded admin untouched, and the corresponding `admin_users` rows cascade off through migration 0002's foreign key.

The baseline/restore contract snapshots ids the suite can write: `routes` and `fare_configs` ids from the test database and `%@komyuter.test` auth user ids from the main database; restore deletes test-database routes and fare configs whose ids are not in the baseline (or every row when a baseline list is empty), relying on route cascades to directions → stops → detours → restrictions, and deletes `%@komyuter.test` auth users from the main database, where the auth service created them outside the app's transaction. Because the test database is created within the same run, its route and fare-config baselines are normally empty.

destroyTestDatabase() drops `komyuter_test` with force as the final teardown step, so no test data survives a run; an interrupted run therefore leaves an orphan test database and stray main-database auth users, both repaired by the next run's recreation and sweep — the lifecycle's entry point cleans up whatever its exit point missed.

testDatabaseUrl() clones `DATABASE_URL` and rewrites only the pathname to `/komyuter_test`, making the test database a sibling of the dev database in the same local Postgres instance and keeping credentials, host and port; `createTestDb()` wraps that URL in drizzle, while `createTestPool()`/`createDevPool()` are standalone `pg` pools for the setup and teardown SQL the app never issues.

The test seam is the injectable `buildApp(deps: AppDeps)` taking `{ db, supabase, env }`, the same function production wires with `createDb(env.DATABASE_URL)`, `createSupabaseAdmin(...)` and `loadEnv()`. `buildTestApp(envOverride?)` supplies `createTestDb()` plus a service-role Supabase client, `envWith(overrides)` re-runs `loadEnv` merged over `process.env`, and every integration request goes through `app.inject` so no port is ever bound.

tests/integration/helpers.ts loads `.env` via `process.loadEnvFile` when present and calls `loadEnv()` at module scope, so a missing or invalid `apps/server/.env` fails during file collection with `Invalid environment: …` rather than inside an individual case; the integration half therefore requires the local Supabase stack running plus that `.env` file.

Integration auth is real while integration data is isolated: `signInAdmin()` signs the seeded admin in through `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword` using `ADMIN_EMAIL`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `createTestAdmin()`/`createNonAdminToken()` create confirmed users through the service-role admin API and add the test database's stub `auth.users` + `admin_users` rows, and the route guard calls `supabase.auth.getUser(token)` before checking `admin_users` in the app's `db` — which is the test database.

Build-level configuration is exercised per case by rebuilding the app overrides: `ALLOW_DEV_CREDENTIAL=false` refuses the documented dev credential with the unified denial while `true` accepts it, and the origin guard rejects a foreign `Origin` with the 403 envelope while an allowed Origin, a missing Origin and an `OPTIONS` preflight all pass.

The CRUD integration file pins write/read reflection and refusal semantics end to end: a created route is listed, defaults to inactive and has a zero direction count, an update is visible without a restart, and a delete really removes the row (404 on re-read); directions-with-stops creation, `409` when deleting a stop referenced as a direction terminal, `422` for empty stop lists and invalid LineStrings, detour loop/off-path/degenerate/negative-distance/duplicate-label refusals, atomic detour-stop persistence with cascade on detour delete, and restriction-index range errors.

Fare-configuration lifecycle guards are integration-tested with configs the suite creates itself: deactivating a config referenced by an active route or the sole default is refused with `409`, deactivating one referenced only by an inactive route is allowed, updates that would leave the default config inactive or the system with zero defaults are refused, a deleted (inactive) config cannot be made default, and the list reports `active_route_count` counting only active routes.

The plotting-save integration file pins the two-direction model: `POST` saves the base direction and derives the return in one atomic operation (reversed polyline, reversed stop order renumbered from 1, terminals resolving inside the return's own stop list), a single-stop save or a path whose start does not match the first stop is refused with `422` and persists nothing, a third active direction is refused with `409`, `PUT` with stops and polyline replaces the base and re-derives, route detail returns the base direction before the derived return, and the overview endpoint returns every route's base/return polylines and stops in one request.

Status and persistence are asserted against a real database: `/api/status` reports `ok` with numeric route/stop/direction counts that do not decrease after a create, and a route written through one app instance is readable from a freshly built instance — restart equivalence that makes the database, not process state, the source of truth.

The export integration cases validate the emitted dataset against an Ajv-compiled JSON Schema read from the spec tree (`specs/001-local-supabase-backend/contracts/export-dataset.schema.json`, compiled once and cached; `ajv` and `ajv-formats` are apps/server devDependencies) in addition to asserting the download headers, `schema_version` 1.1, `coordinate_order` `lng_lat`, base and derived-return directions with their own stops, no dangling terminal references, no `eta`/`arrival`/`departure` key anywhere in the body, and a schema-valid dataset that parses standalone even on a fresh database.

The integration half contains a local performance gate: two cases issue twenty `/api/status` reads and twenty export reads and require at least 19 of 20 to complete under one second each, so a loaded machine can fail the suite.

The unit half is database-free and socket-free: its files import only `src/domain/*`, `src/api/throttle`, `src/api/errors`, `src/config/env`, `src/api/mapbox` and the `@komyuter/shared` schemas, substitute ambient dependencies explicitly (an injected `now` for the throttler, an explicit source object for `loadEnv`, `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", …)` for the Mapbox route), and register routes on a bare `Fastify()` instance.

The unit half is where the derivation and coordinate invariants are enforced: `derive.test.ts` pins reversing coordinates without mutating the input, never reusing the base stop or location objects, renumbering `stop_order` from 1, keeping the first stop leading on a closed loop, the `To {first stop name}` label, distance math and `pathEndpointsOnStops` accept/reject cases; `geometry.test.ts` pins `[lng, lat]` bounds with per-coordinate issue paths, rejection of non-finite or non-geometry payloads, and the two-point minimum for LineStrings.

Three more unit files pin domain contracts without a database: `export.test.ts` fixes the dataset shape (`schema_version`, `coordinate_order: "lng_lat"`, conversion of string-mode numeric columns, stop sorting by `stop_order`, empty-database arrays, `referenceCheck` dangling terminal ids, absence of ETA/arrival/departure keys), `validation.test.ts` exercises the detour on-line tolerance including the boundary and the `Detour loop start` / `Detour loop end` / `degenerate` refusal messages, and `schemas.test.ts` pins the `@komyuter/shared` slug and create-schema rules the API validates with.

Because the single config declares `globalSetup` unconditionally and there is no second config or script, any invocation of the suite — including a unit-only path filter — first recreates and migrates `komyuter_test` and afterwards restores the baseline and drops the database; there is no database-free way to run the suite.

The Mapbox proxy is covered only by unit cases that call `registerMapbox` on a bare `Fastify()` instance with no central error handler (the 422 assertion reads `body.error?.code ?? body.code`), resolve `loadEnv(process.env)` per request for `MAPBOX_SECRET_TOKEN`, and stub global `fetch`: they pin the straight-line fallback with `warning: "no_token"`, the snapped-geometry success path, and the `upstream_error` fallback, while no integration case exercises `/api/admin/mapbox/directions`.

The server suite is deliberately outside CI: the workflow runs format:check, lint, typecheck, the admin suite and build, and its comment states that apps/server's integration half needs a live Supabase stack so it stays a local pre-merge obligation; AGENTS.md records `pnpm --filter server typecheck` and `pnpm --filter server test` as mandatory before commit, with tests written first per the repository's spec workflow, and root `pnpm test` (`turbo run test`) still executes the server suite.
